attacks.claim: The budget math is off by about 30x. The $1,140 input figure is one day of logs (2.28B tokens x $0.50/1M), not one month. Over 30 days input alone is about $34,200, roughly 23x the $1,500 approved budget. Output is about $7/day (~$210/month), not $7/month. The plan's ~$1,150/month total and its claim that it fits the budget are wrong.
attacks.evidence: "Input: 38M lines x 60 tokens = 2.28B tokens -> ~$1,140" and "Output: 8,640 x 400 = 3.5M tokens -> ~$7" and "Estimated total: ~$1,150/month, within the $1,500 budget."

attacks.claim: Spend is unbounded and scales with log volume, which rises during incidents. Peak-day volume (61M lines, ~3.66B input tokens, ~$1,830/day input) would breach budget even with corrected math. There is no token cap, sampling, batching, spend alarm, or kill switch.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: per-day or per-month spend cap, line-volume limit, spend alerting. "Application logs: 38M lines/day average across 30 services (peak day 61M)." and "forwards every application log line to the summarizer queue"

attacks.claim: The central cost input of 60 tokens per log line is asserted without measurement. Logs with stack traces, JSON, or request metadata often run well above that, so the cost model may be far off.
attacks.evidence: "Average line length: ~60 tokens after redaction." ABSENT: tokenizer count or sample measurement from production logs.

attacks.claim: The input estimate counts only log tokens. It omits the fixed prompt, re-sent on every one of the 8,640 daily calls, and any retries or PagerDuty-triggered extra calls.
attacks.evidence: "sends the last 5 minutes of logs per service to the LLM with a fixed prompt" and "Input: 38M lines x 60 tokens = 2.28B tokens"

attacks.claim: The 12 eng-week estimate assumes both engineers are 100% available, but the context says on-call/interrupt work averages 50% of their time. Effective build capacity is closer to 6 eng-weeks, so the 6-week schedule is roughly 2x optimistic.
attacks.evidence: "Staffing: both platform engineers full-time for 6 weeks (2 x 6 = 12 eng-weeks)." vs. context: on-call/interrupt work "averages 50% of their time"

attacks.claim: The redaction claim covers only emails, tokens, card numbers and IPs. Free-text PII (names, phone numbers, customer or account IDs, payload fragments inside error messages) is not covered, yet all of it would go to a third-party LLM. The 'audited in Q1' claim covers retention policy, not redaction efficacy on the content sent to Corvid, and is not linked to evidence.
attacks.evidence: "already masks emails, tokens, card numbers and IPs for our log retention policy (audited in Q1)" ABSENT: evidence that the audit tested redaction on model-bound content, or a list of uncovered fields.

attacks.claim: There is no data minimization. log-tap forwards every application log line from 30 services to an external model, with no limits on fields, levels, or services.
attacks.evidence: "subscribes to the existing Vector pipeline after the redaction stage and forwards every application log line to the summarizer queue"

attacks.claim: Summaries and the PagerDuty auto-comment copy log-derived content into new stores (Postgres and a third-party incident system) with no retention period, access control, or secondary redaction. Summaries can quote log fragments, so these stores inherit the PII risk.
attacks.evidence: "stores a structured summary (top errors, new error signatures, affected endpoints, suspected deploy)" and "the PagerDuty incident gets an auto-comment with the latest summaries"

attacks.claim: The plan does not state whether the zero-retention setting and DPA-0417 cover this exact data flow, including training use and sub-processors. The DPA is cited as signed, so this is a scope-verification gap rather than a demonstrated gap.
attacks.evidence: "Corvid account has zero-retention enabled; data processing addendum signed by Legal (ref DPA-0417)."

attacks.claim: The eval replays 40 historical incidents through the LLM, but the plan does not say whether those logs are post-redaction, what retention applies, or who can see them during commander grading.
attacks.evidence: "Before launch, replay the last 40 incidents: for each, generate the summary that would have been attached at page time"

attacks.claim: log-tap feeds a live Vector pipeline with no stated isolation from the summarizer queue. If the queue or LLM call backs up, Vector could block or drop application logs, degrading the observability on-call depends on.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: backpressure, buffer bound, or drop policy for log-tap to summarizer queue. "forwards every application log line to the summarizer queue"

attacks.claim: No timeout, retry, backoff, circuit breaker, or missed-window policy is specified for the Corvid dependency. A slow or rate-limited vendor leaves 5-minute windows unsummarized with no defined outcome.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: failure handling for "every 5 minutes, sends the last 5 minutes of logs per service to the LLM with a fixed prompt"

attacks.claim: There is no 'summary unavailable' or staleness state. A stale, missing, or failed summary attached at page time can be read as current, or its absence can be read as a healthy summarizer.
attacks.evidence: "the PagerDuty incident gets an auto-comment with the latest summaries" with no freshness timestamp, staleness threshold, or failure label

attacks.claim: Incident-time load is not sized. Log volume and summarizer load rise during the incidents when the tool matters most, and the plan sizes only average and peak daily volume with no burst or queue-depth analysis.
attacks.evidence: "Application logs: 38M lines/day average across 30 services (peak day 61M)" with no burst or incident-load capacity analysis

attacks.claim: No observability is specified for the new system: no SLIs or alerts for summary lag, per-service success rate, queue depth, or summarizer liveness. It can fail silently for days, and dashboards are scheduled last.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: metrics and alerting for summarizer health. "Hardening, dashboards, runbook | 2"

attacks.claim: PagerDuty comment failure behavior is unspecified: API errors, rate limits, duplicate comments on retry, and the fallback when the service catalog lookup fails.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: error handling for "PagerDuty integration + service catalog" and the "auto-comment ... (from the service catalog)" step

attacks.claim: The 'within seconds of a page' goal conflicts with the 5-minute summarization cycle. The latest summary at page time can be up to 5 minutes stale, and no latency measurement for the on-page attachment exists.
attacks.evidence: "every 5 minutes, sends the last 5 minutes of logs per service" vs. "summary within seconds of a page" ABSENT: prototype latency measurement.

attacks.claim: The eval does not test the core value claim. The 70% useful gate is one commander grading 40 incidents, with no baseline, no inter-rater agreement, and no test of the 'suspected deploy' or dependency outputs. The claimed MTTR 47 -> 30 min improvement is never measured, and the thresholds are unjustified.
attacks.evidence: "Launch gate: >= 70% useful, <= 5% misleading." and "Target: median MTTR 47 min -> 30 min within one quarter of launch." ABSENT: MTTR baseline methodology or control comparison.

attacks.claim: A 5-minute window of all logs per service has no truncation, sampling, or chunking rule. During incidents a service can spike to thousands of lines, so the summary may be truncated or fail exactly when it is most needed.
attacks.evidence: "sends the last 5 minutes of logs per service to the LLM with a fixed prompt" ABSENT: context-limit or truncation handling.

attacks.claim: There is no feature flag or runtime kill switch for the summarizer or the page-time comment. Misbehavior or a spend spike can only be stopped by a code rollback.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: feature flag or runtime disable. "Summaries are advisory only" describes intent, not an operational control.

attacks.claim: The LLM's structured output is stored with no schema validation or parse-failure handling. Malformed or partial JSON could be attached to incidents undetected.
attacks.evidence: "stores a structured summary (top errors, new error signatures, affected endpoints, suspected deploy)" with no validation step

attacks.claim: The model is not version-pinned and has no fallback. Pricing and quality are assumed, and a fixed prompt compared against eval results is sensitive to silent model changes.
attacks.evidence: "Model: Corvid-mini, $0.50 per 1M input tokens, $2.00 per 1M output tokens." ABSENT: pricing reference, version pin, or fallback model.

attacks.claim: 'Advisory only' conflicts with auto-commenting into the PagerDuty incident, which on-call reads under time pressure. A misleading summary can anchor responders on a wrong cause.
attacks.evidence: "Summaries are advisory only." alongside "the PagerDuty incident gets an auto-comment with the latest summaries"
